info.title: Unikraft Cloud Network Shield Plugin API
info.description:
This specification describes the Network Shield plugin API, the control API
of a network shield instance on Unikraft Cloud. It manages the policies that
say what the sandboxes behind the shield may reach and what may reach them,
the secrets the shield substitutes into their requests and the limits on the
shield as a whole, and it reports what is enforced and what the control
plane has done.

Every operation declares a single `default` response: the standard response
envelope, which carries the outcome of the request in `status`, the
human-readable reason for a failure in `message` and the HTTP status code in
`errors`. The HTTP status code itself distinguishes success from failure; the
status codes an operation can return are documented on the operation.

A failure whose reason has structure carries it in `data` instead, with
`message` empty. There are three: a body that fails validation (`422`), whose
`data` lists each field at fault as `type`, `loc` and `msg` and never the
value it held; a write to a shield that has sealed (`503`), whose `data` is
the shield's account of what failed, as `error`, `reason`, `failures`,
`sealed` and `remedy`; and a bandwidth limit the host could not apply
(`500`), whose `data` is `error` and `failures`. A path no operation serves
is `404`, and a method an operation does not take `405`, both enveloped.

get.description: Get the limits in force, read back from the kernel.

put.description:
Set the limits. `422` is returned for a rate that is not a multiple of 8,
or out of range, and `500` when the host could not apply it, in which case
the cap before stays in force.

default.description: The limits as they now stand.

get.description:
Read the log of what the control plane did, a page at a time, oldest
first; the latest entries are `order=desc&count=N`. Each category keeps
its 10,000 most recent entries. `422` is returned for a `count` out of
range, an `order` other than `asc` or `desc`, a `from` that is neither an
id nor a time, or a query parameter this operation does not take.
List every policy in force, in the order they were written.

put.description:
Replace the whole policy set. A policy whose id is in both keeps its
counters, address sets and listener where the change leaves them meaning
the same thing. `409` is returned when an id appears twice, and `422` when
the set is refused: a policy fails validation, two policies collide, the
set needs more address sets or listeners than the shield has, or it would
leave a secret bound to a policy that is gone, or substituting into none.

default.description: The policy set as it now stands.

post.description:
Add policies, as an array even of one, which is added whole or not at all.
`201` is returned with the policies added. `409` is returned when an id is
taken or appears twice, and `422` when the addition is refused.

get.description: Get one policy by id. `404` is returned when no such policy exists.

put.description:
Replace one policy, in place, leaving the others as they are. The policy
and the set it leaves are checked as a whole-set replace checks them, and
a refused replace changes nothing. A request counter is kept while the
port keeps a request limit; a connection allowance is kept while the
port's rule is unchanged, and starts full when the limit's numbers change.
`404` is returned when no such policy exists, and `422` when the body
names another id or the change is refused.

default.description: The policy as it now stands.

delete.description:
Delete one policy. `404` is returned when no such policy exists, and `409`
when a secret is bound to it, or substitutes into nothing else.

default.description: The outcome of deleting the policy.

get.description: List every secret in force. Values are never returned.

default.description: Every secret in force, values excluded.

put.description:
Replace every secret. A stored secret may leave out its `value` to keep
it. `409` is returned when an id appears twice, and `422` when a secret is
refused: it fails validation, is new and has no value, is bound to an
`http`, `passthrough` or missing policy, no `https` policy it is bound to
covers its hostnames, or the set holds more than 100.

default.description: The secrets as they now stand, values excluded.

post.description:
Add secrets, as an array even of one, which is added whole or not at all.
`201` is returned with the secrets added. `409` is returned when an id is
taken or appears twice, and `422` when a secret is refused.

get.description: Get one secret by id. `404` is returned when no such secret exists.

put.description:
Replace one secret, leaving the others as they are. Its value is replaced
when the body gives one, and kept when the body leaves `value` out. It is
in force when the request is answered. `404` is returned when no such
secret exists, and `422` when the body names another id or the secret is
refused as an added one would be.

default.description: The secret as it now stands, value excluded.

delete.description: Delete one secret. `404` is returned when no such secret exists.

default.description: The outcome of deleting the secret.

get.description:
Get the state of the shield: what is enforced, which generations the proxy
has loaded, and whether the shield has sealed.

This operation is also the plugin's readiness probe: it takes no
parameters, changes nothing, and answers on a shield with no policies and
on one that has sealed. Hence `x-unikraft-plugin-readiness`, which the SDK
generators read to render their readiness helpers against this operation.

LogsQuery.category.name: category
LogsQuery.category.description: (OPTIONAL) Only the entries of this category.

LogsQuery.from.name: from
LogsQuery.from.description:
(OPTIONAL) Where the page starts: an ISO-8601 time, meaning the first
entry at or after it, or with `order=desc` the last at or before it. A time
without a zone is UTC, and a number is refused. The oldest entry by
default, or with `order=desc` the newest.

LogsQuery.order.name: order
LogsQuery.order.description: (OPTIONAL) Oldest first, or newest first. The default is oldest first.

AddressConflict.description: An address two policies on one port have resolved under two handlers.

AddressSets.description: The address sets the policy set needs, against the kernel's table.

max_bits_per_second.description: The cap, a whole number of bytes per second: a multiple of 8.

BandwidthLimit.description: A cap on what the shield sends to the sandboxes, in bits per second.

max_connections.description: New connections allowed within the window. Over it they are reset.

window_seconds.description: The window: a second, a minute, an hour or a day.

ConnectionLimit.description: A cap on new connections, counted by the kernel, on any handler.

ConnectionLimited.description: A connection limit, for one policy and port.

Direction.description: Which way the connections a policy applies to go.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

EmptyResponse.description:
A response which carries no data of its own. `data` is `null`; the outcome of
the request is the HTTP status code.

ipset.description: Whether the kernel matches address sets; no policy is enforced without.

intercepted.description: Redirects into the proxy, one per policy and port.

passthrough.description: Exemptions from the proxy, one per policy, port and protocol.

connection_limited.description: Connection limits, one per policy and port.

inbound.description: Sandbox ports opened by inbound policies.

address_conflicts.description: Addresses claimed under two handlers on one port. Normally empty.

sets_near_capacity.description: Address sets near capacity. Normally empty.

address_sets.description: The address sets needed, and the most the kernel holds.

error.description: Present only when the fields above could not be worked out: why.

bandwidth_limit.description: The shield-wide bandwidth cap in bits per second, or `null`.

Enforcement.description: What the packet layer enforces, derived from the policy set.

Exemption.description: An exemption from the proxy, for one policy, port and protocol.

Handler.description: How the connections a policy matches are carried.

secrets.description: The generation of secrets the proxy has loaded, or `null`.

limits.description: The generation of request limits the proxy has loaded, or `null`.

IcapGenerations.description: The snapshot generations, published and loaded by the proxy.

sandbox.description: The sandbox's name as the policy gave it, or else its address or range.

address.description: The sandbox's address, or the range of sandboxes.

port_range.description: The ports opened, both ends included: one port is a range of one.

listener.description: `http` only: the listener serving the policy, else `null`.

sources.description: `http` only: the networks clients may connect from; empty is anyone.

InboundPort.description: A sandbox port an inbound policy opens.

handler.description: The proxy listener it goes to.

Intercept.description: A redirect into the proxy, for one policy and port.

bandwidth_limit.description: (OPTIONAL) The bandwidth cap; absent or `null` for none.

Limits.description: The limits on the shield as a whole, rather than on a policy.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

LimitsResponse.description: The response carrying the limits, read back from the kernel.

timestamp.description:
When the event occurred, in UTC to the microsecond. No two entries share
one, so it is also the entry's place in the log.

uptime_ms.description:
The control plane's uptime when the entry was written, in whole
milliseconds. It drops when the control plane restarts.

message.description: What happened, sanitised and at most 2048 characters.

details.description: Structured detail, which varies by category.

logs.description: The entries, in the order asked for.

next.description:
The `from` of the page after this one: a microsecond after the last
entry's `timestamp`, or with `order=desc` a microsecond before it, and
`null` with `order=desc` once the oldest entry is on the page. In
ascending order it is set after the newest entry too, so that asking with
it returns what has been written since, and an empty page answers with
the `from` it was sent.

total.description: The entries from `from` on, before `count` cuts the page.

server_time.description: The shield's time when it answered.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

LogsResponse.description: The response carrying a page of the log.

policies.description: The policies, in the order they were written.

PolicyListData.description: Policies: every one in force, or for an addition the ones added.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

PolicyListResponse.description: The response carrying the policy set.

hosts.description:
(OPTIONAL) Hostnames, each with at most a single leading `*.` wildcard,
stored lowercased. Not addresses, which go in `networks`. Inbound: the
sandbox's private name, exactly one.

networks.description:
(OPTIONAL) IPv4 networks in CIDR notation, given by their network address.
Outbound: public ranges only. Inbound: the sandbox's address, which a name
in `hosts` is resolved to when the policy is written, or on a passthrough
policy a range of sandboxes. A policy names a host or a network.

ports.description:
The ports to match. A policy names at least one port, here or in
`port_ranges`. On an outbound policy 53 and 3128-3131 are reserved.

port_ranges.description:
(OPTIONAL) Ranges of ports, both ends included. An inbound passthrough
policy's only, for the platform's plugin range.

protocols.description: (OPTIONAL) The protocols to match; `tcp` when empty.

sources.description:
(OPTIONAL) Inbound `http` only: the IPv4 networks clients may connect
from, read from `X-Forwarded-For`. Empty admits anyone.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

id.description:
The policy's id: 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, but not
`.` or `..`, unique among the policies.

handler.description: How matched connections are carried; inbound, `http` or `passthrough`.

request_limit.description: (OPTIONAL) A cap on requests. Not on `passthrough`, nor inbound.

connection_limit.description: (OPTIONAL) A cap on new connections. Not inbound.

PortRange.description: An inclusive range of ports; one port is a range of one.

id.description: (OPTIONAL) The policy's id. Given, it has to be the path's.

handler.description: How matched connections are carried; inbound, `http` or `passthrough`.

request_limit.description: (OPTIONAL) A cap on requests. Not on `passthrough`, nor inbound.

connection_limit.description: (OPTIONAL) A cap on new connections. Not inbound.

ReplacePolicyRequest.description: The request to replace one policy, which the path names.

id.description: (OPTIONAL) The secret's id. Given, it has to be the path's.

value.description:
(OPTIONAL) The value substituted for the pattern. Left out, the stored one
is kept. Never returned.

inject.description: Where and how it is substituted.

hostname.description:
Exact hostnames the secret may be substituted for, at least one, at least
one of them covered by an `https` policy the secret is bound to.

bound_to_policies.description:
(OPTIONAL) The `https` policies whose requests the secret is substituted
into. Empty, it applies to every `https` policy covering its hostnames.

ReplaceSecretRequest.description: The request to replace one secret, which the path names.

max_requests.description: Requests allowed within the sliding window; over it, 429.

window_seconds.description: The length of the sliding window, in seconds.

RequestLimit.description: A cap on requests, counted by the proxy, on `http` and `https` policies.

status.description: The HTTP status code of the error.

ResponseError.description: The error response message for an API request.

ResponseStatus.description: The response status of an API request.

sealed.description: Which of the shutdown steps took effect.

remedy.description: What to do: replace the instance.

Sealed.description: Why the shield sealed. Once set, it never clears.

id.description: The secret's id, on the same terms as a policy's.

value.description: The value substituted for the pattern. Never returned.

inject.description: Where and how it is substituted.

hostname.description:
Exact hostnames the secret may be substituted for, at least one, at least
one of them covered by an `https` policy the secret is bound to.

bound_to_policies.description:
(OPTIONAL) The `https` policies whose requests the secret is substituted
into. Empty, it applies to every `https` policy covering its hostnames.

header_name.description:
The request header the pattern is replaced in. Only what HTTP allows in a
header name: letters, digits, any of !#$%&'*+-.^_|~ and the backtick.

pattern.description: The literal text replaced by the secret's value.

SecretInject.description: Where and how a secret is substituted.

SecretListData.description: Secrets: every one in force, or for an addition the ones added.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

SecretListResponse.description: The response carrying every secret's metadata.

inject.description: Where and how it is substituted.

hostname.description: The hostnames it may be substituted for.

bound_to_policies.description: The policies it is bound to.

SecretMetadata.description: A secret as the API answers it: everything but the value.

id.description: The secret's id, on the same terms as a policy's.

value.description:
(OPTIONAL) The value substituted for the pattern. Left out, the stored one
is kept; a new secret needs it. Never returned.

inject.description: Where and how it is substituted.

hostname.description:
Exact hostnames the secret may be substituted for, at least one, at least
one of them covered by an `https` policy the secret is bound to.

bound_to_policies.description:
(OPTIONAL) The `https` policies whose requests the secret is substituted
into. Empty, it applies to every `https` policy covering its hostnames.

SecretReplacement.description: A secret as a replace of every secret sends it.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

SecretResponse.description: The response carrying one secret's metadata.

policy.description: The policy the set belongs to.

port.description: The port the set belongs to.

SetNearCapacity.description: An address set at 90% of its capacity or above.

uptime_ms.description: Whole milliseconds since the control plane started.

policy_count.description: The number of policies in force.

secret_count.description: The number of secrets in force.

failed.description:
`null` while the shield can say what it enforces. Set when applying a
policy set failed: the shield denies all traffic and refuses every write.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

StatusResponse.description: The response carrying the state of the shield.

servers.description: A control plane running locally, listening on its default port
The netshield plugin route of a shield running on a Unikraft Cloud metro

metro.description: The metro the shield is running in, e.g. `fra`.
